summary.description: PCBs are colourless or yellow oily liquids or solids with no odour, mainly used as electrical insulating materials in capacitors and transformers and as flame retardants.
emission_sources: Leakage during disposal of PCB-containing equipment
environmental_impact: Toxic to humans causing damage to brain, eyes, heart, immune system, kidneys, liver, reproductive system, skin, and thyroid gland
May cause cancer and harm unborn children
Highly toxic to wildlife, especially aquatic organisms, causing reproductive and developmental problems
Persistent organic pollutant (POP) leading to long-term environmental contamination

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: PCBs have serious health impacts on humans, including cancer risk and damage to multiple organs and systems, threatening overall wellbeing.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: PCBs are highly toxic to aquatic life, causing reproductive and developmental harm, severely impacting marine biodiversity and ecosystem health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Due to their persistence and toxicity, PCBs contaminate water bodies, compromising clean water sources and sanitation.
